body:
The recent changes in #815 introduce two PDF versions. Is this correct? I have attached the two versions here for ease of reference. 

New version: [OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 4.x2.pdf](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/files/7355912/OWASP.Application.Security.Verification.Standard.4.x2.pdf)

Existing version: [OWASP Application Security Verification Standard 4.x.pdf](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/files/7355913/OWASP.Application.Security.Verification.Standard.4.x.pdf)

comments.body:
I created two versions hoping to have a discussion as to which is better. One version uses Eisvogel for creating it. That's a latex template for creating nice-looking documents. The other one is plain latex.

As a side note, markdown is converted to latex and from latex the PDF is created. 

My preference is with the version that uses Eisvogel, even if it introduces an extra dependency. With the build environment in a docker container this dependency is transparent for the end user.

We can also discuss what we want to have in the headers and footers.

Please look at the both document versions and let me know which one you prefer.

Eisvogel looks very useful, and I'm inclined to use it since it has a lot of heavy-lifting templating variables we shouldn't have to maintain ourselves. 

Perhaps if we came up with a list of aspects of the original PDF design that are either important or appreciated, then we could make sure the new template incorporates those aspects. Who would be a good person to help us make that list?

Otherwise, I'd be happy to just start running with the new template using Eisvogel and call it good.

I'll change the makefile and remove the unnecessary header file. I will
then make a pull request.

Now we need to discuss what we would like to see in the header and footer.

Please take a look at the generated PDF and let me know what you think
about it as it is.
